chunks: ‘Ali ibn al-Ḥusayn narrated to me from Sa’d ibn ‘Abdillāh, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ‘Īsā, from ‘Abd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Najrān, who said:

I asked Abā Ja‘far (peace be upon him), ‘What is the reward for those who go to the Ziyārah of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) with the (sole) intention of Ziyārah?’ He replied, ‘(Their reward is) Paradise. And whoever goes to the Ziyārah of the grave of Abī al-Ḥasan (peace be upon him), for him is Paradise.’
ai.seo_question: What is the reward for visiting the grave of Imam al-Kazim?
ai.summary: This hadith from Ibn Qulawayh records a direct chain from Imam al-Kāẓim (a.s.) equating the reward of visiting the Prophet with that of visiting his grandson, Imam al-Kāẓim, thereby elevating the status of the Imams as spiritual successors. Historically, this underscores the Shia emphasis on the continuity of divine guidance through the Ahl al-Bayt, where physical visitation serves as a tangible connection to the spiritual authority of the Imams. The promise of Paradise for both signifies that Ziyārah is not merely a ritual but a means of affirming allegiance (Walayah) to the Prophet’s lineage.

en.sayyid-mohsen-al-husayni-al-milani: 12. ‘Ali ibn Ḥusain narrated to me from Sa’d ibn ‘Abdillāh, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ‘Isā, from ‘Abdil Raḥmān ibn Abī Najrān, who said:

I asked Abā Ja’far (Imam Jawād (a.s.)), “What is the reward for those who go to the Ziyārah of the Prophet (s.a.a.w.) with the (sole) intention of Ziyārah?” Imam (a.s.) replied, “(Their reward is) Paradise and the reward for those who go to the Ziyārah of the grave of Abil Ḥasan (Imam Kāżim (a.s.)) is (also) Paradise.”
